SKILLS PLAN:

* zimmerMANNPreBuild
   * the gate at the start of coding work
   * the planner
   * checks everything for the task
   * checks all resources
      * JIRA - user story, details, requirements, ACs, linked design, attachments, linked work items, and activity (comments)
         * flags anything missing, misaligned, needing clarification, etc.
      * Confluence - check for anything that could help or relate to the user work (TSDs, docs, etc.)
         * flags anything missing, misaligned, needing clarification, etc.
      * Local File - context and knowledge base for FED UI Build
         * flags anything missing, misaligned, needing clarification, etc.
      * Codebase - check the state of the codebase in preparation for the build
      * Design/Figma - look into the designs: complete (all variants, states), tokenization, responsiveness (viewports)
         * flags anything missing, misaligned, needing clarification, etc. 
         * if the actual design nodes links are needed (in case the main figma file/design links are not enough), ask for them to be supplied by the developer
   * creates the full plan
      * closed-loop multi-agent workflow
         * multi-commit or multi-branch depending on the scale of work
      * end to end plan - full execution
   * hands-off to the zimmerMANNBuild skill
   * RUNS CLAUDE OPUS 5 ON MAXIMUM EFFORT
* zimmerMANNBuild
   * the builder
   * the executioner
   * the implementer
   * executes the full plan
      * closed-loop multi-agent workflow
         * multi-commit or multi-branch depending on the scale of work
   * hands off to the zimmerMANNPostBuild skill
   * after PR has been opened, work will resume here for change requests from CodeRabbit or Tim then back to zimmerMANNPostBuild
   * RUNS CLAUDE SONNET 5 ON MAXIMUM EFFORT
* zimmerMANNPostBuild
   * my own Senior Dev
   * checks, audits, analyses what's been built
   * checks zimmerMANNBuild's work against zimmerMANNPreBuild's findings
   * does the commits, pushes, and PRs
   * when CodeRabbit in the GitHub PR returns change requests or Tim provides change requests himself, the work will be handed back to zimmerMANNBuild for fixing and back to here when the changes have been done for committing, pushing, and replying to the CodeRabbit and/or Tim change request comments
   * RUNS CLAUDE SONNET 5 ON MAXIMUM EFFORT
* zimmerMANNReview
   * reviews others' PRs / code
   * implements the same work as zimmerMANNPreBuild + zimmerMANNBuild + zimmerMANNPostBuild but tailored for code review (gather, test/check/audit, review)
   * when the change requests are verified and validated, creates general and inline comments in the PR
   * loops until the PR is approved (changes are pushed, re-run review)
* zimmerMANNDevImprover
   * is run at the end of build work to run a full check/audit/analysis into the session, take the learnings for improvement of build works that will be done moving forward, and improve zimmerMANNPreBuild + zimmerMANNBuild + zimmerMANNPostBuild accordingly and as applicable
* zimmerMANNRevImprover
   * is run at the end of review work to run a full check/audit/analysis into the session, take the learnings for improvement of review works that will be done moving forward, and improve zimmerMANNReview accordingly and as applicable
* zimmerMANNDevOps
   * has full/complete knowledge of the pwa kit repo's dev ops
   * has full/complete knowledge of the current state of the pwa kit repo / codebase
   * will run deploys, release cuts, tagging, releases etc.
* zimmerMANNSprinter
   * will be the skill i use during sprint/agile ceremonies
      * sprint planning
      * sprint daily standups
      * sprint backlog refinements
      * sprint retrospectives
   * has full/complete knowledge of the JIRA board, Confluence, and Trello

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

## ac642cf1-e1c8-4490-9caa-814476453870
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_f

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- claude-md-management:claude-md-improver: Audit and improve CLAUDE.md files in repositories. Use when user asks to check, audit, update, improve, or fix CLAUDE.md files. Scans for all CLAUDE.md files, evaluates quality against templates, outputs quality report, then makes targeted updates. Also use when the user mentions "CLAUDE.md maintenance" or "project memory optimization".
- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Routes to a direction-specific reference doc; loads alongside `figma-use` for the code → design path.
- figma:figma-use: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)

- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file

Yes — both, for both Zimmermann repos. Two separate access routes, and it's worth knowing the difference:

**1. The app's session index** (MCP session tools)
`list_sessions` / `search_session_transcripts` / `list_events` — full-text search across transcripts and read any one of them. Returns **53 named sessions**, ~46 of them Zimmermann (`ZIMM - PR #70`, `ZIMM - Contentful Setup`, `ZIMM - Guardrails`, etc., back to `ZIMM - Dev Onboard Checklist` on 2026-07-15). **This index does not include agent sessions.**

**2. Raw transcripts on disk** (`~/.claude/projects/`) — this is the exhaustive one

| | zimmermann-pwa | Zimmermann-Handover |
|---|---|---|
| Top-level sessions | **399** (987 MB) | **119** (379 MB) |
| Sessions that spawned agents | 46 | 15 |
| Agent transcripts | **268** | **41** |
| Range | 2026-07-09 → today | 2026-07-13 → today |

Agent sessions live at `<session-uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` with a `.meta.json` sidecar carrying `agentType`, `description`, and `spawnDepth` — so I can tell *what each agent was asked to do* without reading its whole transcript. Breakdown for pwa: 199 `general-purpose`, 65 `Explore`, 2 `Plan`, 2 `fork`.

**Two caveats worth flagging:**

- **53 vs 399.** The sidebar index only tracks named sessions; forks, resumes, and short/untitled ones exist only as files. If you mean *all* sessions, I have to work from disk, not the session tools.
- **1.4 GB total.** Far beyond what I can load. So it's search-and-excerpt, not read-everything — I grep for what you're after and pull the relevant spans. Works well; just means I need a reasonably specific target.

What are you trying to pull out of them?

content.text:
Scanned all 399 pwa-kit sessions plus the 268 agent transcripts. Your read on the pattern is correct — but the data says something you may not expect, so let me lead with that.

## You already built this plan. Six weeks ago.

`zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills/` has **14 skills** in it, dated Jul 15 – Aug 19. Well-written ones, with real descriptions.

Across 399 sessions there were **85 Skill invocations total** — about 0.2 per session. And:

| Skill | Invocations |
|---|---|
| `code-review` | 28 |
| `session-start` | 22 |
| `code-quality` | 12 |
| `pr-checklist` | 11 |
| `generate-changelog` | 3 |
| **`audit-tier`, `scope-check`, `new-component`, `feature-spec`, `qa-generate`, `onboarding`, `project-init`, `contentful-register-component`, `upstream-sync-review`** | **0** |

Nine of fourteen have never fired once. `session-start` — whose own description says *"use at the start of every coding session"* — fired in 22 of 399 sessions. About 5%.

So "build a set of skills I reach for" is not an untested idea. It's a tested one, and the reaching-for is where it broke. Building fourteen more gets you twenty-eight skills and eighty-five invocations.

## Why the five survivors survived

The ones that stuck all share a shape: **a named deliverable at an unmistakable moment.** "Review this PR." "Write the PR description." You *know* you're at that moment, so you reach.

The nine that died split into rituals (`session-start`, `project-init`, `onboarding`) and scaffolds (`new-component`, `audit-tier`, `scope-check`). A ritual you have to *remember to invoke* isn't a ritual — it's another thing to remember, which is the exact fatigue you're trying to remove.

## The bigger gap: your #1 workload has no skill at all

Clustering how your sessions open:

| Workload | Sessions |
|---|---|
| **Research → verify → report** (codebase + Confluence + Jira) | **116** |
| Branch / repo hygiene | 95 |
| Jira ticket / user story work | 82 |
| PR / code review | 30 |
| Meeting prep & in-meeting capture | 28 |

That top row is your job, and you've hand-typed its incantation ~99 times. Verbatim samples:

- `execute an in-depth analysis across the codebase, confluence, and JIRA…`
- `execute an in-depth check of the codebase + confluence + and jira…`
- `execute an in-depth full-on exhaustive check…`
- `execute an in-depth, verbose, and authoritative scan…`
- `execute an in-depth v&v/check/audit into the codebase, codebase docs, codebase config, confluence, and JIRA…`

**That drift is the inconsistency risk you sensed.** Not a missed step — a moving depth setting. "In-depth" and "in-depth full-on exhaustive" are different instructions, so the same question asked twice gets researched to two different standards. Tool counts confirm this is the real workload: ~3,500 Atlassian calls against 26,117 Bash calls. None of your 14 skills touches it.

## The asset you're undervaluing

502 Agent invocations, and their descriptions are remarkable: `Verify guardrail claims to file:line locations`, `V&V doc vs codebase/configs`, `Stage1 validate → Stage2 implement → Stage3 regression verification`, `Wave1 scope ledger` → `Wave2 adversarial reconciliation`, `Agent A/B/C/D` split audits.

You have a genuine claims-must-be-verified-to-file:line discipline, and you're already running staged multi-agent loops by hand. **You don't need to import loop engineering — you're doing it.** What you need is to stop rebuilding the harness from scratch each time.

## What I'd actually do

1. **Fix invocation before authoring.** Anything whose description says "every time" should be a `SessionStart` hook, not a skill — the harness runs it, you don't remember it. That alone converts `session-start` from 5% to 100%.
2. **Write one skill: the research-verify-report loop.** Highest-value single artifact you can produce — 116 sessions of retyping, and it's where the depth drift lives. Bake the depth tiers in (quick / standard / exhaustive) so "how hard should I look" becomes a parameter instead of an adverb.
3. **Then triage the nine dead ones** — some belong as `.claude/rules` (`audit-tier`, `scope-check` are really guardrails), and some may just be genuinely rare and worth deleting.

One caution on loops: they pay off where a **cheap, honest verifier** exists — tests, tsc, lint, CI. Your PR-review and story-shaping work has no such verifier; the verifier is you. Wrapping those in an automated loop mostly buys you confident-sounding iteration. Keep those human-in-the-lead, the way `qa-generate` already says.

Want me to start with the hook conversion and the research-verify-report skill? Or would you rather I first dig into *why* specific dead skills didn't fire — I can pull the sessions where you did that work by hand and see what you typed instead.

Makes sense — and it corrects something in my last message that matters.

**Those skills aren't yours.** `git log` on `.claude/skills/` shows TimLavelle (14 commits), Hardi (13), TimLavelleACC (5). Zero from you. So "you already built this plan" was wrong — they're a team artifact, committed to the repo, encoding Tim's and Hardi's model of the codebase. You not reaching for them isn't a discipline lapse; they were never built around your process.

Which makes the invocation data read differently, and better for your case: the five that fired (`code-review`, `session-start`, `code-quality`, `pr-checklist`, `generate-changelog`) are exactly the ones that happen to overlap with lead duties. The nine that never fired are IC and setup work — `new-component`, `contentful-register-component`, `qa-generate`, `onboarding`, `project-init`. You didn't skip them; they're not your job. That's a role mismatch, not a fatigue problem, and a personal layer is the correct fix for it.

## The two layers

| | Team layer | Personal layer |
|---|---|---|
| Where | `zimmermann-pwa/.claude/` (committed) | `~/.claude/skills/` (yours, portable) |
| Answers | "How does *this codebase* do X" | "How does *Marcel* work" |
| Owner | Tim, Hardi | You |
| Scope | Dies with the project | Follows you to Handover, and the next client |

Your personal layer is effectively greenfield right now — `~/.claude/skills/` contains only `playwright-skill`.

**One design rule I'd hold to:** personal skills *orchestrate*, team skills and rules *execute*. Your skill should **cite** `.claude/rules/typescript.md` and `.claude/registry/components.md`, never copy their contents. The moment you paste Tim's conventions into your personal skill, you've forked the team's standards into a private copy that silently rots the next time he edits the original — and you'd be reviewing PRs against a stale bar without knowing it. Reference, don't duplicate. That also keeps your skills portable: on the next project they bind to whatever rules exist there.

## Sources, ranked

1. **Your 399 sessions** — the strongest source by far, and the only one that records what you *actually* do rather than what you'd say you do. The ~99 hand-typed research incantations are literally the spec for your flagship skill, drift and all.
2. **`.docs/prompts/`** — worth a look; that may already be you saving your own prompts.
3. **`.claude/rules/` (11 files) + `.claude/registry/` (5)** — not content to absorb, but the things your skills should point at. Note `squadA.md` / `squadB.md` — squad ownership is lead-relevant.
4. **The 14 team skills** — read for mechanics and for the quality bar you're reviewing against.

## What I'd expect the personal set to be

From your own workload distribution, these are all role-shaped rather than codebase-shaped — none of them belong in the team repo:

- **research-verify-report** (116 sessions) — the flagship, with depth as a parameter instead of an adverb
- **pr-review-as-lead** (30) — wraps the team's `code-review`, adds your approval judgment
- **story-shaping / ticket intake** (82)
- **meeting prep & capture** (28)
- **branch & repo hygiene** (95) — possibly just a hook, not a skill

Does that match the set you had in mind, or is your list different? If it's roughly right, I'd start by mining those ~99 research prompts into a single spec — that's the one where the evidence is richest and the repetition cost is highest.

DEV = os.path.expanduser("~/Dev")

]

# sibling-file cross-references -> in-document part references.
# NB: zimmermann_frontend_lead_playbook.md is a RETIRED external doc; never rewrite it.
XREF = [
    (re.compile(r'`uiBuild-knowledge\.md`\s*(§\d+)'), r'Part I \1'),
    (re.compile(r'`fedBuild-manual\.md`\s*(§\d+)'),   r'Part II \1'),
    (re.compile(r'`fedLead-playbook\.md`\s*(§\d+)'),  r'Part III \1'),
    (re.compile(r'`uiBuild-knowledge\.md`'),          r'Part I'),
    (re.compile(r'`fedBuild-manual\.md`'),            r'Part II'),
    (re.compile(r'`fedLead-playbook\.md`'),           r'Part III'),
]

def slug(s):
    s = s.strip().lower()
    s = s.replace("&", "").replace("§", "")
    s = re.sub(r"[^\w\s-]", "", s)
    s = re.sub(r"[\s_]+", "-", s)
    return re.sub(r"-+", "-", s).strip("-")

def process(path, drop_companion_block):
    """Demote headings by one level, drop the H1, rewrite sibling xrefs.
    Fence-aware so '#' comments inside code blocks are never touched."""
    lines = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n")
    out, toc = [], []
    fence = None
    dropped_h1 = False
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        ln = lines[i]
        m = re.match(r'^(\s*)(`{3,}|~{3,})', ln)
        if m:
            tok = m.group(2)[0]
            if fence is None: fence = tok
            elif fence == tok: fence = None
            out.append(ln); i += 1; continue

        if fence is None:
            if not dropped_h1 and re.match(r'^# ', ln):
                dropped_h1 = True; i += 1
                continue
            # drop the now-meaningless "Companions:" pointer block
            if drop_companion_block and ln.startswith("**Companions:**"):
                while i < len(lines) and lines[i].strip() != "":
                    i += 1

            h = re.match(r'^(#{2,5}) (.*)$', ln)
            if h:
                lvl, txt = len(h.group(1)), h.group(2)
                if lvl == 2: toc.append(txt)
                ln = "#" * (lvl + 1) + " " + txt
            for pat, rep in XREF:
                ln = pat.sub(rep, ln)
        out.append(ln); i += 1
    return "\n".join(out).strip("\n"), toc

doc = []

I assembled it mechanically rather than retyping, so content loss was structurally impossible, then verified line-by-line: **every substantive line from all three sources is present.** Word count 16,666 → 17,179 (+513, entirely the new preamble and TOC).

**Structure** — one H1, then:

| | Source | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| Part I — UI Build: Knowledge & Context | `uiBuild-knowledge.md` | 77–846 |
| Part II — FED Build Manual | `fedBuild-manual.md` | 847–1657 |
| Part III — FED Lead Playbook | `fedLead-playbook.md` | 1658–2451 |

**What I changed** (only the seams):

- Headings demoted one level — H1 doc → H2 part → H3 section → H4 subsection. Zero level skips. The demotion is fence-aware, so `#` comments inside code blocks were left alone.
- **7 cross-references** rewritten from filenames to part refs: `` `uiBuild-knowledge.md` §7 `` → `Part I §7`, and the tier-1 table row → `see Part III`.
- **3 `Companions:` blocks** dropped — they pointed at sibling files that are now sections.
- Added a preamble + linked TOC covering all 45 sections.

**Deliberately preserved:** the two `zimmermann_frontend_lead_playbook.md` references — that's the *retired* doc, not a sibling, so rewriting them would have been wrong. All `[CORRECTED]` markers and per-document revision footers are intact.

**Three calls I made that you may want different:**

1. **Filename** `fed-handbook.md` — trivial to rename.
2. **Part order** follows the order you listed them (knowledge → procedure → role). That's bottom-up; for reading, role-first is usually better, though for grep-as-a-source it barely matters.
3. **Originals untouched** — all three still sit in `~/Dev`. I didn't delete anything. Worth deciding whether they stay as the editable sources with the handbook regenerated, or whether the handbook becomes canonical and they retire.

The regeneration script is at `scratchpad/merge.py` if you want to re-run it after editing the sources.

One note for what's next: the "Authority on styling" line now appears in the preamble *and* twice inside the parts. I left the in-part copies for fidelity, but when we mine this for skills, that's exactly the sort of thing the skill should point at `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` for rather than restate.

## 2. The 11 rules files

### `overrideStyling.md` (280 lines) — the authority on the build approach

The single most prescriptive file. **The styling hierarchy, in reach-for order (`:12-37`):**
1. `textStyle` prop for anything textual — `textStyle="body2"`, **never a raw `fontSize`**; all 22 Handover text styles live in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never a bare Chakra/theme token key** (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) even though it resolves identically — house-style, for unambiguity at the call site. Mechanically enforced for recipes by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`; **that guard cannot see the same mistake in a JSX/`sx` prop** — that half is manual (`:24-27`).
3. The component's own theme config — `theme/components/<name>.ts` **or** co-located `<name>.css.ts`.
4. `sx` for a one-off prop-system gap.
5. Scoped `.scss` only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors, keyframes).

**"Never: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file"** (`:39`). One standing exception: `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional `BTN_HEIGHT_LG/SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`. `npm run audit:tokens` (`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`) greps for exactly this across `overrides/app/components/**` and `overrides/app/theme/components/**`; a hit is downgraded when the surrounding comment contains `provisional|pending|placeholder|audit-allow: <reason>`. **Not wired into CI** (`:50`, restated `:227-237`) — 14 pre-existing violations need triage first.

**Units (`:58-70`):** `rem` for anything scaling with root font-size (type + spacing, WCAG 1.4.4); `px` for hairline geometry that must *not* scale (borders, focus-ring offsets); `em` only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts`).

Other hard constraints:
- **Alias tier is a reference, not a copy** (`:72-87`) — semantic tokens read from primitive consts; `zimmTokens.ts` derives everything except 7 numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases.
- **One canonical styling surface per component type** (`:89-104`) — a component's theme config is the single source of truth; **do not also give it a `.zimm-*` global class**, because a static class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/`_focusVisible`. `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*`; use Chakra `<Button>`.
- **Importing an already-overridden component (`:106-134`) — a real trap.** From component A, import an already-overridden B by **relative path** (`'../swatch-group'`), *not* the SFCC base path, because the `ccExtensibility` resolver only runs in the real app build — Storybook aliases straight to `node_modules` and Vitest doesn't touch it, so a base-path import silently renders/tests the **unstyled base SFCC version**. Known unfixed instance: `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice` import (`:126-130`).
- **Component-local tokens (`:136-165`)** — reference the foundation entry as `var(--zimm-*)`, not `2`, not `'0.5rem'`, not the bare key. **Responsive steps are explicit media queries keyed off `BP`, not Chakra's array shorthand** — the guard walks responsive arrays and fails every element. No existing foundation entry and no confirmed Figma value → **leave it inherited; don't invent a number**.
- **SFCC bridge pattern (`:173-193`)** — if SFCC's own base components import it, the default export stays a faithful undecorated port (full prop surface, same `forwardRef`); Zimmermann styling goes behind a named export (the `product-tile` `CardBaseline` split).
- **Co-location governance (`:197-250`)** — `theme/components/` is Tier 2 gated to the UI designer, but CODEOWNERS' `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` routes a co-located recipe to the owning squad only, dropping the designer gate. Explicit **known inconsistency flagged not resolved** (`:218-225`): `zimmButton.css.ts`'s unapproved provisional constants are no longer designer-gated while still keying the app-wide `Button` recipe. Cross-file shared values go in a small module that stays in `theme/components/` (e.g. `footerShared.ts`).
- `:252-266` logs known gaps; `:268-281` logs follow-up initiatives (per-component CSS loading; `globalStyles.ts` adoption is near zero).
- ⚠️ `:4` cross-references `./overrides.md` — **that file does not exist in `.claude/rules/`**.

### `css.md` (74 lines)

Day-to-day companion. `:9-46` Tokens — no hardcoded hex, no px spacing, no raw font sizes; shows three code examples including the ❌ bare-token case. `textStyle` is the one deliberate bare-key exception because there's no `var()` substitute for the composite expansion (`:26-31`). `:33-46` states plainly that the raw-value half has a script but **no CI gate and no `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` rule**, while the bare-token half **is** enforced via `recipeGuards.test.ts` on every `npm run test`.

`:48-74` `.scss` only when Chakra props are insufficient, with 6 hard constraints: filename matches the component exactly; **scoped and co-located only, no global stylesheets outside `overrides/app/theme/`**; **nesting depth ≤ 3**; **no ID selectors**; **no `!important` without an inline reason comment**; prefer `sx` or a theme variant over a new `.scss` file.

### `components.md` (167 lines)

- **Components (`:11-47`):** named export matches folder name, no anonymous default exports; props type named `<Component>Props`; **placement default = top of the component file**, move to `types.ts` only on *shared consumption* (not line count alone); JSDoc required on ≥2-caller components, every exported hook, and non-obvious utils; `onEventName` callbacks; optional props use `?`, no `| undefined` unions.
- **Accessibility (`:35-47`) — "mechanically enforced by `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`":** every `<img>` needs `alt` (`alt=""` fine for decorative); every `IconButton` (incl. `IconButtonWithRegistration`) needs `aria-label`; any non-native element with `onClick` (`div`/`span`/`Box`/`Flex`/`Stack`/`VStack`/`HStack`/`Grid`/`Text`) needs a `role`, plus `tabIndex={0}` and `onKeyDown` for real operability.
- **Composition (`:49-104`):** ~150 lines / ~10-15 cyclomatic complexity as a self-check — **explicitly NOT ESLint-enforced today** (`:56-58`). **Container/presentational separation (`:62-90`)** is the big one: anything under `overrides/app/components/` receives data as props and calls **no** data-fetching hook (SDK *or* React Query); fetching lives in `overrides/app/pages/` or a container. Narrow exception for Context-backed app-wide static-content hooks (`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) — with a precise warning that their no-Provider behaviour **differs**: `useUiCopy` degrades to fallback text, `useIntl` **throws**, and its `IntlProvider` is mounted by base SFCC `_app` not `_app-config`, so Vitest tests must wrap it. Extract-to-hook triggers: ≥2 related `useState` that change together, or any `useEffect` with a non-trivial dep array/cleanup; ≥4 `useState` is a coarse "stop and ask".
- **Hooks (`:106-113`):** `.ts` only (no JSX), exported name matches filename, params and return typed, JSDoc with `@returns` mandatory.
- **Storybook (`:116-166`):** story **required** for anything exported from its folder under `components/` or `pages/`; **not required** for single-parent internal sub-components; pages get one full-assembly story. Seven-category table (`:137-143`) `Foundation/ Elements/ Layout/ Commerce/ Forms/ Pages/ Contentful/` with a tiebreaker rule and ✅/❌ examples. Every file has a `Default` export; named exports for meaningful states only; `play` only when there's interactive behaviour worth asserting.

### `testing.md` (432 lines) — the largest rules file

- **Three layers, no duplication** (`:3`), with a long carve-out (`:5-20`): this is **not** license to skip a component's own test file because a hook test or a parent's `play` covers it transitively. Resolve duplication by *scoping what the file asserts* (mock the hook/child proven elsewhere; test only this component's render-branch/event-wiring contract). Reference: `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx`. Exempt: components with no branching at all (`BottomBar`).
- Layer table `:22-26` — Vitest / Storybook `play` / Playwright, each gated on every PR via `qa.yml`; BrowserStack multi-browser on `release/**`.
- **What to test / skip (`:32-44`):** ✅ data mapping, integration boundaries (Global-e pricing/tax, checkout ownership branching, consent gating), complex state, refactor-invisible logic. ❌ re-exports, visual snapshots in Vitest, the framework itself.
- **Vitest (`:46-97`):** co-located, **`.test.ts` suffix, never `.spec.ts`**; describe/test, Arrange-Act-Assert, behaviour-named tests, `vi.clearAllMocks()`. Mock the smallest surface; **MSW allowed for cross-module integration tests but never in production paths**; don't mock the thing under test. **Known gap (`:79-86`): `ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest** — mock it at the smallest surface; unfixable from a test file because the SVG transform lives in Tier 1 `vitest.config.ts`. Commerce SDK hooks need `QueryClientProvider` + `CommerceApiProvider` via a `renderWithProviders` helper in `overrides/app/test-utils/`.
- **Storybook `play` (`:99-137`):** always query via `within(canvasElement)`, never `document`; **`getByRole` with accessible name first**, then `getByLabelText`, then `getByText`; import `userEvent` from `@storybook/test`, not `@testing-library/user-event`.
- **Playwright (`:139-416`):** gherkin-first three-stage workflow, no Playwright code until Lead QA signs off. Fixed `e2e/` layout. Naming `SFCC-NNN_short-description.<priority>.spec.ts`; Jira-less smoke = `SMOKE-{area}-{behaviour}.spec.js`.
  - **Change-scoped E2E (`:168-206`)** — `develop`-targeted PRs only. Areas: `homepage, checkout, search, account, pdp, plp, integrations`. A changed file outside a single area's allow-list resolves to `e2e_scope: skip` and **`e2e-localhost` does not run at all** (changed 2026-08-25). Documented as a **deliberate accepted coverage trade-off**, not a gap to work around. `release/**` PRs always run the full suite.

Five generated markdown tables + two hidden JSON caches. Every `.md` carries the header `> Generated by \`node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs\` — do not edit manually.` plus a timestamp and `> Base: @salesforce/retail-react-app@10.0.0`.

| File | Lines | Columns |
|---|---|---|
| `components.md` | 101 | Component, Origin (Base/Override/Custom), Path, Props, **Tier**, **Squad**, **Consumers**, Last touched, Description |
| `hooks.md` | 71 | Hook, Origin, Path, Description, Consumers, Tier, Squad, Last touched |
| `utils.md` | 39 | Utility, Origin, Path, Exports, Last touched, Description |
| `pages.md` | 25 | Page, Origin, Path, Squad, Tier, Last touched |
| `routes.md` | 26 | URL, Component, Page folder, Source (Override/Inherited), Squad, Tier — generated from `overrides/app/routes.tsx` + inherited base routes |

**Generation** — `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` (header at `:1-16`): full run (`npm run generate:registry`, also run on `postinstall`), incremental `--file=PATH`, or `--fresh` to ignore caches. It computes and stamps Tier and Squad onto every row — i.e. the registry is the **materialised join of the tier/squad rules against the actual file tree**.

The script's own comment documents a fixed bug where incremental mode used to blank every untouched row in a category to `—`.

**Consumption** — two skills read it and both degrade gracefully: `feature-spec/SKILL.md:39` ("_If `.claude/registry/` exists_, read components.md, hooks.md, utils.md", else `find`), and `generate-changelog/SKILL.md:49-53` (`git diff BASE..HEAD -- .claude/registry/` to detect new assets, else `git log --diff-filter=A`). ## 5. Skill-to-skill invocation and subagent spawning

### Two distinct mechanisms

**(a) Prose convention — what superpowers actually ships.** There is *no* frontmatter field for chaining. It's plain markdown text using the `plugin:skill` canonical name. **(b) Structural — `context: fork` + `agent:`.** The engine-native way to make a skill *be* a subagent, from the extracted schema:

Zero installed skills use this. It is schema-confirmed only — but it is almost certainly what you want for a "this skill runs isolated on a cheap model" design, combined with `model:`/`effort:`.

### Subagent dispatch as expressed in practice

`dispatching-parallel-agents/SKILL.md` — parallelism is a *turn-shape* rule, not an API:
```text
Subagent (general-purpose): "Fix agent-tool-abort.test.ts failures"
Subagent (general-purpose): "Fix batch-completion-behavior.test.ts failures"
Subagent (general-purpose): "Fix tool-approval-race-conditions.test.ts failures"
```
> Multiple dispatch calls in one response = parallel execution. One per response = sequential.

`subagent-driven-development/` ships **prompt-template files beside SKILL.md** — `implementer-prompt.md`, `task-reviewer-prompt.md`, `re-review-prompt.md` — plus `scripts/sdd-workspace`, `scripts/task-brief`, `scripts/review-package`. The flowchart references them as relative paths (`./implementer-prompt.md`, `../requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md`). That `../` is notable: **cross-skill file references by relative path work.**

Its model-selection guidance is the manual equivalent of a per-skill effort field:
> **Always specify the model explicitly when dispatching a subagent.** An omitted model inherits your session's model — often the most capable and most expensive — which silently defeats this section.
> ...**Turn count beats token price.** Wall-clock and context cost scale with how many turns a subagent takes, and the cheapest models routinely take 2-3× the turns on multi-step work — costing more overall.

## 6. Progressive disclosure

The three-level model, from `plugin-dev/skills/skill-development/SKILL.md`:

> 1. **Metadata (name + description)** — Always in context (~100 words)
> 2. **SKILL.md body** — When skill triggers (<5k words)
> 3. **Bundled resources** — As needed by Claude (Unlimited*)
>
> *Unlimited because scripts can be executed without reading into context window.

Convention: `scripts/` (executable, may run without entering context), `references/` (loaded on demand), `assets/` (used in output, never loaded). Target **1,500–2,000 words** for SKILL.md, hard ceiling ~3,000. Referencing style:
```markdown
## Additional Resources
### Reference Files
- **`references/patterns.md`** - Common patterns
- **`references/advanced.md`** - Advanced use cases
```

Superpowers uses a flatter convention (`writing-skills/SKILL.md`):
> **Separate files for:** 1. **Heavy reference** (100+ lines) — API docs, comprehensive syntax. 2. **Reusable tools** — Scripts, utilities, templates. **Keep inline:** Principles and concepts, code patterns (< 50 lines).

**(a) Prose convention — what superpowers actually ships.** There is *no* frontmatter field for chaining. It's plain markdown text using the `plugin:skill` canonical name. ### Subagent dispatch as expressed in practice

`dispatching-parallel-agents/SKILL.md` — parallelism is a *turn-shape* rule, not an API:
```text

Subagent (general-purpose): "Fix batch-completion-behavior.test.ts failures"
Subagent (general-purpose): "Fix tool-approval-race-conditions.test.ts failures"
```
> Multiple dispatch calls in one response = parallel execution. One per response = sequential.

That `../` is notable: **cross-skill file references by relative path work.**

Its model-selection guidance is the manual equivalent of a per-skill effort field:
> **Always specify the model explicitly when dispatching a subagent.** An omitted model inherits your session's model — often the most capable and most expensive — which silently defeats this section.
> ...**Turn count beats token price.** Wall-clock and context cost scale with how many turns a subagent takes, and the cheapest models routinely take 2-3× the turns on multi-step work — costing more overall.

## 6. Progressive disclosure

The three-level model, from `plugin-dev/skills/skill-development/SKILL.md`:

> 1. **Metadata (name + description)** — Always in context (~100 words)
> 2. **SKILL.md body** — When skill triggers (<5k words)
> 3. **Bundled resources** — As needed by Claude (Unlimited*)
>
> *Unlimited because scripts can be executed without reading into context window.

Convention: `scripts/` (executable, may run without entering context), `references/` (loaded on demand), `assets/` (used in output, never loaded). Target **1,500–2,000 words** for SKILL.md, hard ceiling ~3,000. Referencing style:
```markdown
## Additional Resources
### Reference Files
- **`references/patterns.md`** - Common patterns
- **`references/advanced.md`** - Advanced use cases
```

Superpowers uses a flatter convention (`writing-skills/SKILL.md`):
> **Separate files for:** 1. **Heavy reference** (100+ lines) — API docs, comprehensive syntax. 2. **Reusable tools** — Scripts, utilities, templates. **Keep inline:** Principles and concepts, code patterns (< 50 lines).

# The Zimmermann UI build pattern — extracted from PR #56 and PR #59

---

## Part 1 — PR #56: `refactor(theme): zimmTokens single source of truth + var(--zimm-*) consistency`

**Merged** 2026-08-18 · branch `feature/theme-token-consistency` · 17 files, +705/−462 · author `TimLavelleACC`

### 1a. Body and review conversation

The body frames five concerns, each a *drift-closure* argument rather than a feature:

1. `zimmTokens.ts` "made fully derived" from `colour.ts`/`spacing.ts`/`typography.ts`/`sizes.ts` "instead of hand-retyped literals, closing a drift risk that previously had only a Vitest test as a safety net."
2. `button.ts` established as "the single source of truth for button styling" — `globalStyles.ts`'s parallel `.zimm-btn-*` class system deleted outright because it had "real value conflicts (different heights, transparent-vs-opaque secondary background, zero interactive states)."
3. `header.ts`/`listMenu.ts` brought onto `var(--zimm-*)`; untokenised values "flagged with a comment rather than silently retimed."
4. New `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` (178 lines, net-new) documenting the resulting hierarchy.
5. px → rem conversion for WCAG 1.4.4, px retained only for hairline geometry.

The body also names the *deliberate scope-down*: `link.ts` excluded because "the component doesn't exist on `develop` yet — separate PR", plus `f2r/`, CI work, demo deletions, and a cosmetic formatting diff. And: "All referenced `var(--zimm-*)` tokens were confirmed to already exist on `develop`'s `zimmTokens.ts` before branching."

**Review conversation.** Three PR-level comments, nine reviews. The Protected File Guard bot posted the Tier 2 notice for `navConstants.ts`, `button.ts`, `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`. CodeRabbit produced exactly **one actionable inline nitpick** and **two `vendor.d.ts` findings**:

- *Nitpick, fixed*: "Centralise the unresolved navigation letter-spacing value. Both files hardcode the same prototype value." → resolved by creating `overrides/app/theme/components/navConstants.ts` (5 lines) holding `NAV_LETTER_SPACING`, imported by both. Commit `4fce726`.
- *Two `vendor.d.ts` findings, declined with a written rationale on-thread*. The author's reply is the template for how declines are done here — it names the reason, the rule, and the follow-up:

  > "Not acting on either: the `Link`/`NavLink`/`useParams` ambient types were added ahead of the Link component override … that component is deliberately excluded from this PR … Adding `@types/react-router-dom` is a new devDependency, which per this repo's AGENTS.md Hard Rule 7 needs integration-team approval — out of scope for this PR to just add. Will revisit … in the Link-component follow-up PR, scoped to whatever props that component actually uses."

- One finding *was* fixed rather than deferred (the loose ambient types with `state: any`), and the body says so explicitly: "a CodeRabbit finding on this PR's own diff, fixed rather than deferred."

### 1b. File-level diff shape, grouped by concern

| Concern | Files |

| Token derivation | `foundation/zimmTokens.ts` (+133/−118), `colour.ts` (+83/−70), `typography.ts` (+123/−89), `spacing.ts` (+25/−13), `sizes.ts` (+4/−3), `foundation/index.ts` (+2/−2) |
| Single-surface enforcement | `theme/globalStyles.ts` (+6/−88 — the `.zimm-btn-*` deletion), `theme/components/button.ts` (+35/−38) |
| Convention alignment | `theme/components/header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`, new `navConstants.ts` |
| Regression net | `theme/index.test.tsx` (+27/−12) |

### 1c. Commit sequence

```
1  63dfe00  refactor(theme): apply zimmTokens single-source convention to header, listMenu
2  2381909  chore(coderabbit): exclude f2r/ from AI review scope
3  5b36062  refactor(theme): make zimmTokens.ts fully derived, button.ts the single source of truth

What the order reveals: **the convention is applied to an existing consumer first (1), before the source of truth is restructured (3).** Commit 1 proves the `var(--zimm-*)` convention works against real recipes; only then does commit 3 rewrite `zimmTokens.ts` to be derived and delete the competing class system. Commit 4 is a single dedicated review-response commit, not amendments folded back. Every commit body carries a *why*, and commit 2's body records the Tier 1 identity verification inline:

> "Tier 1 file (coderabbit.yaml) — verified via `gh api` that the authenticated identity (TimLavelleACC) is a member of @ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers before making this change, per AGENTS.md's Tier 1 Approval verified-session exception."

## Part 2 — PR #59: `feat(footer): SFCC-55 global footer UI`

**Merged** 2026-08-24 · branch `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui` · merge commit `8362b3c` · 132 files, +8724/−1187

### 2a. Body

The body is structured to *pre-empt review friction*. Sections: Description → three "points worth surfacing before review" → Linked (ticket, Figma node, sign-off names + date, test-case IDs) → Squad ownership → Types of Changes → Changes (grouped by concern with the rationale inline) → How to test-drive → **Protection-tier check** → Testing checklist.

Two paragraphs from "Changes" carry the load-bearing architectural decisions:

> "`theme/components/footer.ts` — the `ZimmFooter` multipart recipe. Named `ZimmFooter`, not `Footer`: `extendTheme` deep-merges, so a recipe sharing a base SFCC recipe's name inherits it rather than replacing it"

> "`components/ui-kits/` — six atoms/molecules; `cssVars` indirection removed in favour of the `--zimm-*` custom properties directly, and `utils/cssVars.ts` deleted"

The Protection-tier check block names each protected path, its tier, its owner, and the authorisation basis — including "Authenticated as `marcelannavarro`, a member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`." The Testing block is 9 checked lines with counts (`168/168`, `15 play functions across 7 stories`, `112 footer elements × 6 viewports, 0 off-token paddings`, `axe 0 violations / 17 passes`).

The body also **flags pre-existing defects it is not fixing** (`header/index.tsx`'s `fontSize="l"` and `useCurrentBasket`) and **flags mechanical noise** ("9 of the 16 new commits carry `.claude/registry/` churn … Mechanical — skip those hunks").

### 2b. Review conversation

- **179 inline comments** across **57 top-level threads**: 118 from `coderabbitai[bot]`, 61 replies from `marcelannavarro`. Plus 17 PR-level comments and 136 review submissions.
- Two auto-bots fire first: the Protected File Guard (Tier 2 notice listing all 17 shared files including every `.css.ts`) and the MRT preview-environment deploy.
- CodeRabbit auto-paused reviews ("branch under active development"); the author drove it manually with `@coderabbitai review` / `full-review` / `resolve`.

**How findings were resolved.** Every thread got an in-thread reply — this is mandated by AGENTS.md ("A fix commit alone, with no reply posted on the thread, doesn't count"). Three resolution modes:

*Fixed, with the mechanism explained and blast radius stated:*
> "Fixed in `706e47d`. Rather than adding a component-level JSDoc, `extractDescription` now takes the row's own declaration name … Demoting the offending comment was tried first and just handed the row to the next JSDoc down (`NEW_TAB_SUFFIX`) … Blast radius checked before committing: only 2 registry rows moved."

*Fixed, with the finding generalised beyond what was asked:*
> "Fixed in `fce5af1`. `heading === 'Contact'` is gone; the three sites now key off a `showContactChannels` boolean on the group. Verified locale-independent by renaming the fixture heading to `Kontakt` … `CONTACT_GROUP_HEADING` was removed entirely so the string cannot come back."

*Deferred with acceptance criteria, or declined with the rule cited.* The author posted a public round-up comment (2026-08-21T17:23) that reads as the canonical form:
> "**Deferred to HPC-035** with your acceptance criteria noted on the thread: the focus-containment branch in `useSubscribeModal` … Both unreachable while `enableNameCapture` defaults to false. **Deferred to HPC-034:** production values for `phoneHref`, `whatsAppHref` and `emailHref` … **Declined with rationale on-thread:** the `.storybook/` and `foundation/fonts.ts` findings (verified tier-1-approver session per AGENTS.md's Tier 1 Approval section; both comment/config-only, no token changed), and the `header/index.tsx` `fontSize="l"` correction, which predates this branch by two months and belongs to an ast-grep rule rather than a footer PR."

CodeRabbit responded by writing two **persistent learnings** back into its model keyed to this PR. Notably the author also self-corrected mid-review:
> "You were right that this failed CI, and my own check missed it — I grepped case-sensitively for `\"Clear input\"` while the story matched `/clear input/i`."

The highest-value findings that changed the architecture: unsafe-href guard extracted to `overrides/app/utils/safeHref.ts` and shared between footer and `ZimmNavItem`; `showContactChannels` flag replacing English-string matching; `clearable` made opt-in; contact-channel fields added to both the Contentful schema *and* the TypeScript type together.

### 2c. File-level diff shape, grouped by concern

| Concern | Files |
|---|---|

| **ui-kit organisms** | `ui-kits/organisms/{zimmSubscribeModal,zimmSubscribeSection}/` |

| **Utils** | `utils/safeHref.ts` + test, `utils/resolveByRegion.ts` + test |
| **Theme** | `theme/components/index.ts` (+19/−1), `theme/components/footerShared.ts` (+28), `theme/components/button.ts` (**−119, deleted/moved**), `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` (+365), `theme/fontFace.tsx` + test |

| **Fonts** | `static/fonts/*.woff2`, `.storybook/{main.js,preview.tsx}` |

### 2d. Commit sequence — 45 commits

The full sequence is best read as **six phases**. Selected commits with what they reveal:

**Phase 1 — Scaffold (1–8).** `8c25f11 feat(footer): … atoms, molecules, subscribe modal, and Figma token alignment` builds everything inline in one commit. Then a run of `fix(ui-kit)`/`fix(footer)` commits absorbing the first CodeRabbit pass, plus Figma pixel corrections quoting node IDs: `f681d75 … Desktop site-map: flex:1 fill → flex:0 0 600px fixed (Figma node 40000407:11736 w-[600px])`.

**Phase 2 — Token indirection, then its reversal (9–14, 24, 28).** `a2a2af4 refactor(ui-kit): introduce cssVars utility` created `utils/cssVars.ts` exporting `var(--zimm-*)` strings as named constants. Fourteen commits later `78f2236` deletes it:
> "The cssVars object was an indirection over strings that are already the public contract … A recipe reading `cssVars.font.size['3xs']` and one reading `'var(--zimm-font-size-3xs)'` emit identical CSS, but the former hides which variable is in play at the point of use and needs a second lookup to review. Every consumer now names the variable directly, and `utils/cssVars.ts` is deleted rather than left orphaned."

**Phase 3 — Move styling into recipes (15, 18, 21, 29).**
- `dc86c13 refactor(ui-kit): migrate ZimmButton to Chakra Button+button.ts` — "so all interaction states (hover, press, focus, disabled) live in CSS pseudo-props, not React state … remove useState for hovered/pressed/focused".
- `3a37a4c refactor(footer): extract provisional values to _foundation, wire footer.ts theme config` — "connect via `useMultiStyleConfig` — `footer/index.tsx` now uses `chakra.footer`/`chakra.div`/`chakra.button` so colours and localeButton interactive states … come from the theme config rather than inline styles".
- `b231f06 refactor(footer): migrate layout to footer.ts theme config` — "Moves all responsive layout CSS out of the inline `FooterStyles` `<style>` tag into `footer.ts` … removing the `!important` injection-order guards."
- `3220239 refactor(zimm-text-input): move colour derivation from the hook into the theme recipe`:
  > "The recipe is the single styling surface for the component, so a variant or state added later cannot disagree with the hook about what colour applies."

**Phase 4 — Folder taxonomy (17, 39).** `39ad495 refactor(ui-kits): organise components into atoms/ and molecules/ subdirectories`, later extended to `organisms/`.

**Phase 5 — Decomposition (~43–45, the ones that produce the final shape).** `theme/components/footer.ts`'s 33 parts split across five co-located `.css.ts` files plus `footerShared.ts`, and the extraction of `ZimmSubscribeSection`/`ZimmSubscribeModal`/`ZimmModal`/`ZimmContactIconRow` out of the footer's inline JSX.

**Phase 6 — Guards, then coverage (30, 31, 36, 42).** `3ba238e test(theme): add recipe guards and text-input colour coverage`:
> "recipeGuards.test.ts covers three failure modes that produce plausible-looking CSS rather than an error, so nothing else would catch them … **Each guard was verified by mutation: reintroducing the defect fails that guard and nothing else.**"

`ec5bf9b test(ui-kit): cover unsafe-href fallback and input-action validation` — "Mutation-verified: removing the `(?!\/)` lookahead fails it, and so does allowing `javascript:`."

**What the sequence reveals about the intended build order:**
1. Build it working and inline first, pixel-matched against Figma with node IDs recorded.
2. Convert every literal to `var(--zimm-*)` at the point of use. Reject any indirection layer over it.
3. Move every interactive state from React state into the recipe.
4. Move every layout rule from inline `<style>`/`style` props into the recipe.
5. Split the monolithic recipe by component ownership, extracting reusable components out of the parent as you go.
6. Only then write the guards — and mutation-verify each one.

# Part 3 — THE PATTERN

## 3.1 Tokens

**Where they're defined.** `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` — Tier 1, UI-Designer owned, listed in `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md:12-24`. Files: `colour.ts`, `fonts.ts`, `typography.ts`, `gridSystem.ts`, `spacing.ts`, `motion.ts`, `sizes.ts`, `zimmTokens.ts`.

**Two-tier colour, alias-by-reference.** `overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts:1-56` — primitives are private module `const`s, the exported semantic tier reads from them:

```ts
// colour.ts:6-16
const grey = { black: 'black', 900: '#191919', 800: '#282828', … };
// colour.ts:45-55
export const colors = {
  grey, ivory, coral, green, orange, red, opacity,
  background: { '01': ivory[100], '02': ivory[200], … '05': grey[900], … },
```

The rule (`overrideStyling.md`, "The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy"): *"Do the same for any new primitive/alias pair you add — two values can't disagree if only one of them is ever typed."*

**`zimmTokens.ts` is the CSS-var registry, fully derived.** `overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts:1-14`:

```ts
// All --zimm-* variables, derived from the other foundation/* files (the actual source
// of truth, ported from the Figma-to-React work) rather than retyped here.
import { colors } from './colour';
import { fontSizes, lineHeights, letterSpacings, fontWeights } from './typography';
import { spacing, borderWidths, focusRingOffsets } from './spacing';
…
export const zimmTokens: Record<string, string> = {
  '--zimm-color-text-default': colors.text.default,       // :47
  '--zimm-focus-ring': `${borderWidths.default} solid ${colors.border.focus}`,  // composite, :66
```

The only literals left are the 7 numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` Handover aliases with no named-scale equivalent (`'--zimm-scale-700': '28px'` etc.) — documented as "not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to derive them from."

**How they surface as `var(--zimm-*)`.** `overrides/app/theme/zimmTokensGlobal.tsx:16-27` stringifies the registry onto `:root` via a raw Emotion `<Global>` — deliberately *not* Chakra's `styles.global`:

```ts
// zimmTokensGlobal.tsx:7-10
// Deliberately NOT Chakra's styles.global: Chakra's style processor mangles quoted
// font-family values (verified — "'Futura Round', 'Century Gothic', sans-serif"
// collapses to a single family), which would break the --zimm-font-family-* vars.
```

Mounted twice from one definition — `_app-config/index.tsx:159` and `.storybook/preview.tsx` — "so the two mount points cannot drift."

**The usage hierarchy** (`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, "The hierarchy — reach for these in order"):
1. `textStyle` prop for anything textual — never a raw `fontSize`. It is "the one entry in the hierarchy that isn't a colour/spacing token" because there's no `var()` for a composite expansion.
2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` for colour and spacing. Never a bare Chakra/theme key** — `color="text.default"` and `gap="m"` resolve to the *identical* value and are still forbidden. The stated reason is reviewability: *"a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct."*
3. The component's own theme config (`<name>.css.ts` or `theme/components/<name>.ts`).
4. `sx` for a one-off Chakra-prop gap.
5. Scoped `.scss` only when `sx` can't express it.

**Only some foundations are registered as Chakra scales,** and this is load-bearing. `overrides/app/theme/index.ts:29-45`:

```ts
// Registered below: borderWidths, breakpoints, colors, fonts, space, textStyles.
// Deliberately NOT registered, because the Zimmermann scale and the Chakra scale
// use the same key names for different values …
//   fontSizes    Chakra md=16px xs=12px 2xs=10px 3xs=7.2px
//                Zimmermann md=24px xs=16px 2xs=14px 3xs=12px  (4 collisions)
//   sizes        Chakra sizes.lg=32rem vs iconSizes.lg=20px
```

This is why `width: 'xl'` is a real bug, not a style nit — it reads Chakra's `sizes.xl` = 36rem. It shipped a 576px contact icon (`zimmContactIconRow.css.ts:11-16` documents the incident inline).

**Units** (`overrideStyling.md` § Units): `rem` for anything that scales with root font-size (WCAG 1.4.4) — type and the named spacing scale. `px` only for hairline geometry that must *not* scale: border widths, focus-ring offsets. `em` only for breakpoints.

### The rule for when a raw literal is acceptable

`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`: **"Never: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token instead."** With a mechanical downgrade path.

`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` (`npm run audit:tokens`, `package.json` scripts) greps `overrides/app/components/**` and `overrides/app/theme/components/**` for `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.scss`, excluding `*.test.ts(x)` and `*.stories.tsx`:

```js
// scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs:58-60
const HEX_RE = /#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b/g;
const UNIT_RE = /\b\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:rem|em|px)\b/g;
const EXCEPTION_MARKER_RE = /provisional|pending|placeholder|audit-allow/i;
```

**The downgrade rule** (`auditTokenUsage.mjs:20-27`): a match becomes an *acknowledged exception* — printed but not failing — when **the contiguous non-blank block of lines ending at the match** contains `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or `audit-allow`:

```js
// auditTokenUsage.mjs:119-123
let contextStart = idx;
while (contextStart > 0 && lines[contextStart - 1].trim() !== '') contextStart -= 1;
const context = lines.slice(contextStart, idx + 1).join('\n');
const acknowledged = EXCEPTION_MARKER_RE.test(context);
```

The blank-line boundary (not a fixed N-line window) is deliberate, and the header says why: real exception comments here are multi-line blocks covering several sibling declarations, or wrap the marker across a line break — *"A fixed N-line window missed both shapes during this script's own first calibration pass."*

The header also states the rationale for reusing prose as the allow-list: *"This is the exact vocabulary this codebase already uses for every documented raw-value exception today … Reading the existing explanatory comment as the allow-list entry avoids a second, separately-maintained list that would drift from the code the moment either one changes."*

**What a compliant exception actually looks like** — `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts:3-13`:

```ts
// Provisional spacing/size values — kept here as named references until the UI designer
// confirms the token in foundation/spacing.ts or foundation/sizes.ts.
//
// SPACE_SECTION is NOT a missing token: --zimm-scale-1200 (48px) already carries the same
// value. Kept as rem here because that foundation alias is px, which does not scale under
// browser zoom (WCAG 1.4.4 …). Collapse onto the var once the foundation alias moves to rem.
const SPACE_SECTION = '3rem';        // alias/space/section (48px)
const SIZE_COL_SUB = '20rem';        // alias/size/footer/col-width-subscribe (320px)
const SIZE_COL_MAP = '37.5rem';      // alias/size/footer/col-width-sitemap (600px)
const COLOUR_HALF_INV = 'rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.5)'; // alias/color/opacity-50-inverse
```

Note the shape: **named constant + Figma alias path in a trailing comment + a block comment saying what it's waiting on.** Never an inline literal.

`audit-allow:` is for a *permanent* exception where no token will ever exist — `overrides/app/theme/components/footerShared.ts:15-17`:

```ts
// audit-allow: raw em is correct and permanent here, not a placeholder awaiting a token —
// overrideStyling.md's Units section documents breakpoints as one of the few genuinely
// context-relative uses of em, deliberately outside the var(--zimm-*) scale system.
```

Others: `zimmLogo/index.tsx:9-13` (`// provisional` on `LOGO_MAX_WIDTH`/`LOGO_HEIGHT`, with a `§7 raise:` annotation naming the target foundation file and owner); `zimmTextInput.css.ts:26-38` (`PROVISIONAL pending Kiera`); `zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts:6-12` (`PROVISIONAL: … Pending Kiera`); `zimmNavItem.css.ts:5-11` (`No 4.5px entry exists in spacing.ts — same provisional treatment as zimmButton.css.ts's BTN_PADDING_Y`).

**Two separate enforcement mechanisms, do not confuse them** (`overrideStyling.md` says this explicitly): `recipeGuards.test.ts` runs on every `npm run test` and catches *a bare Chakra key standing in for a zimm var*; `audit:tokens` catches *a raw hex/px/rem/em literal*. Neither is in CI as a hard gate for `audit:tokens` — deliberately, pending triage of 14 pre-existing findings.

---

## 3.2 Component taxonomy — atoms / molecules / organisms

**There is no written definition anywhere.** I grepped `.claude/rules/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.docs/architecture.md`, `README.md`: the words `atoms`/`molecules`/`organisms` appear only as *path fragments in examples*. The taxonomy is defined entirely by the code. That's a real gap worth naming.

Here is the rule the code actually follows:

### Atom — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/<name>/`
`zimmButton`, `zimmIcon`, `zimmLogo`, `zimmModal`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmTextInput` (+ later `zimmProduct*`)

Distinguishing property: **an atom composes no other Zimmermann component.** Its imports are React, Chakra, and foundation/icons only. It maps props → one DOM/Chakra element (plus its own decorations).

- `zimmNavItem/index.tsx` — imports only `chakra`, `useStyleConfig`, `isSafeHref`. Renders one `<a>` or one `<button>` with a single `<span>` inside.
- `zimmLogo/index.tsx` — one inline `<svg>`. No Chakra recipe at all; it uses `useToken('colors', …)` because "an SVG `fill` attribute needs a concrete colour value, not a custom-property reference" (`:22-23`).
- `zimmIcon/index.tsx` — a switch over 34 icon types from the icons barrel.
- `zimmButton/index.tsx` — imports `ZimmIcon`, which looks like a violation, but it's a *rendering primitive*, not a composed unit; the file describes itself as "a thin mapping layer: Zimmermann props (inverse, large/medium) → Chakra variant/size names that `zimmButton.css.ts` recognises" (`:7-8`).
- `zimmModal/index.tsx` is the most instructive case: it's a portal + backdrop + dialog panel — structurally large, but classified atom because it **owns no content**: *"Generic modal chrome — portal, backdrop, and an accessible dialog panel. Owns none of the content: a caller supplies its own form/fields as children"* (`:26-27`).

**So: atom = single indivisible UI primitive with no Zimmermann-component children and no domain knowledge.** Size and DOM complexity are irrelevant; `zimmModal` is 64 lines and `zimmLogo` is 80, both atoms.

### Molecule — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/<name>/`
`zimmInputAction`, `zimmContactIconRow` (+ later `zimmProductContent`, `zimmProductMeta`)

Distinguishing property: **composes ≥2 atoms (or repeats one) into a single reusable unit, and may own local UI state — but no business/domain state and no data source.**

- `zimmInputAction/index.tsx:3-5` imports `ZimmTextInput`, `ZimmButton`, `ZimmIconType`. It owns `useState<string|undefined>(validationError)` (`:37`) — pure presentation-level validation, no domain meaning. It has **no `.css.ts`** because it adds no styling of its own beyond `__css={{ display: 'block', width: '100%' }}` on the form (`:60`) — the atoms carry the look.
- `zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx` repeats one atom (`ZimmIcon`) three times with per-channel href logic. It *does* have a `.css.ts` because it introduces its own layout (`row` gap/padding, `iconLink` 24px touch target).

### Organism — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/<name>/`
`zimmSubscribeModal`, `zimmSubscribeSection`

Distinguishing property: **composes molecules/atoms AND binds to a hook that owns a state machine or a feature flow.**

- `zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:47-52` — composes `ZimmInputAction` (molecule) + `ZimmSubscribeModal` (organism), calls `useSubscribeSection(...)` returning `{submitState, modalOpen, closeModal, handleEmailSubmit, handleModalSubmit}`, plus `useUiCopy()` for microcopy, plus its own multipart recipe. It renders a four-state discriminated union (`idle`/`success`/`unavailable`/`error`).
- `zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx` — composes three atoms, calls `useZimmModal({isOpen, onClose})` for focus/scroll/keyboard mechanics, and consumes **two** recipes: `ZimmModal` (chrome, as `chrome`) and `ZimmSubscribeModal` (its own content).

### The extraction test that decides placement
Both organisms and `zimmContactIconRow` state their extraction criterion explicitly in their JSDoc, and it is the same sentence pattern each time — **"nothing here is <parent>-specific":**

> `zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:43-44`: "Extracted from the footer so it can be reused anywhere a storefront needs the same channels — **nothing here is footer-specific.**"

> `zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:30-31`: "**Extracted from the footer so it can be placed on any page**, not just the global footer."

> `zimmModal/index.tsx:28-29`: "Split out of the footer's original SubscribeModal so **any future dialog — not just the subscribe flow** — can reuse the same accessible shell."

By contrast, `FooterNavColumn` and `BottomBar` **stayed in `components/footer/`** as sub-folders, not in `ui-kits/`, precisely because they *are* footer-specific:

> `footerNavColumn/index.tsx:28-31`: "One footer nav column: heading, link list, and (for the Contact group) the contact-channel icon row. Extracted from Footer's inline JSX — **this is where the Figma pixel-precision workarounds below actually live now**, rather than being buried in the footer assembly."

**Governance follows this split:** `CODEOWNERS:176` routes all of `ui-kits/` to *both squads* ("the shared design-system layer consumed by both squads' component overrides"); `CODEOWNERS:87` routes `components/footer/` to both squads + tier-2 + tier-1 approvers.
